content: The Legacy Tobacco Documents Library (LTDL) is a comprehensive digital archive containing over 7 million documents from major U.S. tobacco companies. These documents, spanning the last century, detail the tobacco industry's activities in advertising, manufacturing, marketing, sales, and scientific research. The library was established and is maintained by the University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) Library and Center for Knowledge Management, with funding from the American Legacy Foundation. It serves as a critical resource for researchers investigating tobacco control issues, public health policies, and the industry's strategies regarding smoking regulations, air quality legislation, and cigarette marketing. Journalists, students, and public health advocates also utilize the library to gain insights into the tobacco industry. The UCSF Library Tobacco Documents Bibliography provides examples of publications and scholarly articles based on research conducted using these documents. In 1994, the Attorneys General of Mississippi, Minnesota, West Virginia, and Massachusetts filed lawsuits against the tobacco industry to recover healthcare costs associated with tobacco-related illnesses. Over time, 42 additional states joined these legal actions. The resulting Master Settlement Agreement (MSA) required tobacco companies to make annual payments to the states and imposed restrictions on tobacco advertising and marketing. The MSA also established and funded the American Legacy Foundation, an anti-smoking advocacy group, which in turn funded the creation and maintenance of the LTDL. As part of the MSA, tobacco companies were mandated to release internal documents for public access, both in a physical depository in Minnesota and on their own websites. They were also required to make available any documents produced for litigation on smoking and health until 2008. The National Association of Attorneys General (NAAG) oversees and enforces this operation. In 2002, NAAG provided UCSF with a large collection of document index records and images to create the LTDL. The collection continues to grow through web crawling applications that identify and download records and images directly from tobacco company websites. The LTDL houses internal documents from tobacco companies and trade organizations involved in the MSA, as well as documents from other litigation or companies not part of the settlement. The MSA-mandated collections include materials from American Tobacco, Brown & Williamson, the Council for Tobacco Research, Philip Morris, R.J. Reynolds, and the Tobacco Institute. Additional collections include: UCSF Brown & Williamson Collection: This includes thousands of pages of documents donated to UCSF in 1994, primarily consisting of scientific studies on nicotine addiction and the health effects of tobacco smoke. Brown & Williamson attempted to remove these documents from public access through legal action, but the courts ruled in favor of UCSF, allowing the documents to remain publicly available. Mangini (Joe Camel) Documents: These are internal documents from R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Company, produced during the discovery process of the 1994 civil case Mangini v. R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Company. The documents primarily cover the 1970s to 1990s, a period when R.J. Reynolds developed the Joe Camel advertising campaign. Multimedia Collection: This collection contains over 5,000 video and audio recordings from the tobacco industry, including focus groups, internal corporate meetings, depositions of tobacco industry employees, government hearings, corporate communications, and commercials. Many of these recordings are available for viewing or listening on the Internet Archive. Liggett & Myers Collection: This collection includes approximately 400,000 pages of internal documents from Liggett & Myers (L&M). In 1997, L&M became the first major tobacco company to settle lawsuits in 22 states and provided evidence of industry strategies and tactics to state prosecutors. Due to their early compliance, L&M was not included in the MSA's requirement to create company document websites, making these documents unique to the LTDL and unavailable in electronic format elsewhere. Tobacco Depositions and Trial Testimony Archive (DATTA): This archive contains transcripts from tobacco-related litigation, collected from various sources by the Center for Tobacco Use Prevention and Research in Okemos, Michigan. The 1999 film The Insider provides additional context to the significance of these collections.
